title: Contractor discovery · 30 minutes
opening: I’d like to understand how material purchasing works on your jobs, where it gets difficult, and what you would actually want help with. We’ll use a recent order, then agree on one useful next step.

questions.text: What projects are you running now, and what stage is each one at?
questions.hint: Project type, number of active jobs, next material package. Capture facts, not an assumed contractor profile.
followups: Can you give me a recent example?
Who was involved, and what happened next?

questions.text: Who currently prepares material lists, chooses suppliers and places orders?
questions.hint: GC, office staff, homeowner, designer, subs or a mix. What already works well?
followups: Can you give me a recent example?
Who was involved, and what happened next?

bank.text: What material purchases are coming up over the next month?
followups: Which job needs attention first?
What is already ordered?

bank.text: Who gets pulled away from their main job to handle purchasing?
followups: What do they stop doing?
Tell me about the last time.

bank.text: How does purchasing differ between your new builds, renovations or flips?
followups: Which type requires more coordination?
What changes from job to job?

bank.text: Which suppliers do you rely on, and why?
followups: What do they handle well for you?
Which relationships would you want to keep?

bank.text: Where do your material lists come from?
followups: Does the sub, plan or supplier provide the quantities?
Who checks the final version?

bank.text: How do you establish which materials each sub provides?
followups: Where is that written down?
When was an inclusion last unclear?

bank.text: Who keeps track of the material budget as the job progresses?
followups: How do they spot a change?
What information reaches you too late?

bank.text: Where do you keep quotes, approvals and order details?
followups: How do you find the latest version?
Who else needs access?

bank.text: What limits how many jobs you can manage comfortably?
followups: Where does material purchasing fit into that?
What would another project add to your workload?

bank.text: Tell me about an order that went smoothly.
followups: What made it work?
What should an outside service avoid disrupting?

questions.text: Walk me through your most recent material order, from the first list to arrival on site.
questions.hint: Which material, supplier and people were involved? Ask for the sequence before naming our services.
followups: Can you give me a recent example?
Who was involved, and what happened next?

questions.text: Which part took the most effort or did not go as expected?
questions.hint: Ask what happened, who fixed it and how. If nothing went wrong, record that too.
followups: Can you give me a recent example?
Who was involved, and what happened next?

questions.text: Roughly how much of your time did that order take, and who did you have to contact?
questions.hint: Separate supplier, homeowner/designer and subcontractor calls. Include messages and store trips. Record an estimate or unknown; do not invent a count.
followups: Can you give me a recent example?
Who was involved, and what happened next?

bank.text: How did the request for your last order reach you?
followups: Was the list complete?
What did you have to clarify?

bank.text: How did you decide which suppliers to ask for quotes?
followups: How many did you contact?
Who followed up when a quote did not arrive?

bank.text: How did you check that the quotes covered the same materials?
followups: Were brands, quantities and specifications matched?
How were delivery charges and exclusions handled?

bank.text: When did you confirm stock and lead times?
followups: Did anything change after quoting?
Who found out and handled it?

bank.text: Was an alternative product suggested on the last order?
followups: Who checked whether it would work?
Who approved the change?

bank.text: What homeowner or designer decisions were needed?
followups: Who explained the options?
What happened while you waited?

bank.text: Who actually placed and paid for the order?
followups: How many separate transactions were involved?
What did you still have to check yourself?

bank.text: How were the delivery date and site arrangements agreed?
followups: Who confirmed access and unloading requirements?
Who checked the shipment when it arrived?

bank.text: At what points did this order interrupt your other work?
followups: How long did each interruption take?
Were there store trips as well as calls?

bank.text: Did the materials arrive complete and ready for the work?
followups: What, if anything, was missing?
Who took the next action?

questions.text: Which one or two material packages cause the most repeated work for you?
questions.hint: Use the department selector below. Explore the relevant packages; do not interview all 17 departments in one call.
followups: Can you give me a recent example?
Who was involved, and what happened next?

questions.text: How often does that happen, and what does it affect when it does?
questions.hint: One recent example, events per week/month, GC time, crew waiting or documented extra cost. Distinguish his estimate from verified records.
followups: Can you give me a recent example?
Who was involved, and what happened next?

questions.text: What have you tried to make this easier, and what still falls back on you?
questions.hint: Existing supplier rep, employee, software, sub or another service. What should we preserve?
followups: Can you give me a recent example?
Who was involved, and what happened next?

bank.text: When buying framing materials, where does the process need the most attention?
followups: Who supplies the approved lumber and hardware list?
How are additional framer requests handled?

bank.text: What tends to need clarification on roofing or siding orders?
followups: Are accessories and matching parts on the original list?
Who confirms the approved product and quantity?

bank.text: How do you organize sheetrock and related installation materials?
followups: Who confirms board types, quantities and accessories?
What happened on the last incomplete order?

bank.text: How do window and exterior-door specifications become an approved order?
followups: Who resolves supplier questions with the homeowner?
Who signs off on sizes, options and quantities?

bank.text: What is involved in ordering flooring, tile materials, doors or trim?
followups: Who confirms selections and compatible installation supplies?
Which conversations still need you in the middle?

bank.text: What do you need to understand about materials included in plumbing, electrical or HVAC sub quotes?
followups: Which inclusions or exclusions are unclear?
What information would help you review the material portion?

bank.text: How do you arrange recurring site needs such as dumpsters or temporary supplies?
followups: Which bookings or replacements repeat?
Who checks that the next service is needed?

bank.text: What usually triggers an extra material run?
followups: Was it a changed scope, quantity issue or omitted item?
Who identifies and confirms what is needed?

bank.text: Which purchasing problem has had the biggest consequence recently?
followups: What time or cost can you identify?
Is that from records or an estimate?

bank.text: Which problems are recurring, and which were one-off events?
followups: How many times did each happen on recent jobs?
Which are worth changing first?

questions.text: Who should confirm quantities and specifications, approve spending, and check the delivery on site?
questions.hint: Name each role. Avantia coordinates approved purchases; the contractor/team receives and checks the materials.
followups: What would that look like on the first order?
Who needs to confirm that with you?

questions.text: When your sub needs materials, how would you want the request and approval to reach us?
questions.hint: Direct contact or through GC; who supplies the approved list, who may approve a reorder, preferred channel and spending limit if any.
followups: What would that look like on the first order?
Who needs to confirm that with you?

questions.text: What would you hand over, and what would you prefer to keep handling yourself?
questions.hint: Ask about supplier relationships, homeowner selections and urgent requests. Record concerns and excluded work; do not promise everything.
followups: What would that look like on the first order?
Who needs to confirm that with you?

bank.text: What would a material list need before you would let someone order from it?
followups: Who gives the final approval?
How do later changes get recorded?

bank.text: Which subs would you be comfortable having us contact directly?
followups: What should we discuss without involving you?
What must come back to you for approval?

bank.text: How would you want spending approved?
followups: Is approval needed for each order?
Who can approve when you are unavailable?

bank.text: How should requests for substitutions be handled?
followups: Who checks technical suitability?
Who approves a different price or appearance?

bank.text: What supplier-account arrangements need to remain in place?
followups: Are there terms or relationships we need to preserve?
How would you want orders and payments routed?

bank.text: Who on your team will receive and check deliveries?
followups: How should they report missing items?
What information should accompany that report?

bank.text: How do you want an urgent shortage handled?
followups: Who confirms the item and required timing?
What should happen if the requested timing cannot be met?

bank.text: What updates do you need, and when?
followups: Would you prefer milestones or each change?
Who else should receive them?

bank.text: How should homeowner or designer questions reach the right person?
followups: Which decisions need your involvement?
What would keep you from being the messenger?

bank.text: What would make this service create more work for you?
followups: Which decisions should we never make for you?
What response or availability expectations should we agree on?

questions.text: If we could take only one or two recurring tasks off your plate, which would you choose?
questions.hint: Repeat his words before showing matching Avantia services. Confirm what matters most to him.
followups: What would that look like on the first order?
Who needs to confirm that with you?

questions.text: What would make the first order feel successful enough to use us again?
questions.hint: Choose an observable result: fewer GC calls, less GC time, a complete approved order or a like-for-like price comparison. No guaranteed savings.
followups: What would that look like on the first order?
Who needs to confirm that with you?

bank.text: Which part of purchasing would you most like to stop handling personally?
followups: What would that free you up to do?
What would still need your judgment?

bank.text: Where would a takeoff or material-cost review actually help you?
followups: Would it support your own order or review a sub’s material scope?
Who would verify the quantities before purchase?

bank.text: When is getting another supplier quote worth your time?
followups: What would make a comparison useful?
When would you prefer to stay with the current supplier?

bank.text: Which order tasks would you want handled through one contact?
followups: Calls, purchase arrangements, payments or delivery coordination?
Which of those do you already handle easily?

bank.text: What would a useful shortage and reorder service look like?
followups: Who sends the confirmed missing-item list?
What do you want to stop having to chase?

bank.text: What would you need to see before trusting someone with this work?
followups: Would you want to review each step at first?
What would cause you to stop using the service?

bank.text: What other ways have you considered getting this work done?
followups: Could a supplier rep, employee or sub handle it?
What is missing from those options?

bank.text: How would you decide whether this service is worth paying for?
followups: Which result matters most: time, clarity, fewer interruptions or price?
What would you compare the fee against?

bank.text: If we could help with only one problem first, which would you choose?
followups: Why that one rather than the others?
What could wait until later?

bank.text: What result would you want to measure on the first order?
followups: What is your current baseline, if known?
How would we check the result together?

questions.text: Have I understood the problem and the work you want us to take over correctly?
questions.hint: Read back: problem, department, Avantia action, GC responsibility and success measure. Correct the summary together.
followups: What would that look like on the first order?
Who needs to confirm that with you?

questions.text: What is the next real order we could start with, and what would you need before proceeding?
questions.hint: List/plan/quote needed, person responsible, due date, expected service scope and fee agreement. An interview is not approval to buy.
followups: What would that look like on the first order?
Who needs to confirm that with you?

bank.text: What have I misunderstood or missed about how you work?
followups: Is this your main problem in your own words?
What would you change in the proposed help?

bank.text: Which upcoming material package would make a practical first trial?
followups: Is the approved list ready?
Is the order routine enough to define clearly?

bank.text: What information can you share to start?
followups: Plans, approved lists, supplier quotes or relevant sub scope?
Which version is current?

bank.text: Who needs to be involved in the first order?
followups: Who is the sub or supplier contact?
Who makes the final purchasing decision?

bank.text: Which tasks are included in this first engagement?
followups: Which tasks stay with your team?
What should require a separate agreement?

bank.text: What are the real decision and material-needed dates?
followups: Which dates are fixed and which are flexible?
What still needs confirmation from the supplier?

bank.text: How should we agree on the fee before any work begins?
followups: What scope should the quote cover?
Who needs to approve it?

bank.text: What is still unresolved before you can proceed?
followups: Who can answer each open question?
When should we check back?

bank.text: When should we review whether the trial helped?
followups: What information should each of us bring?
What would justify another order?

bank.text: What is the next action, who owns it, and when will it happen?
followups: What will you send us?
What should we return before you authorize the purchase?

services.name: Takeoff & material cost check
services.when: Unclear quantities or the material portion of a subcontractor quote.
services.question: Who produces and verifies the list today, and which quantity or subcontractor inclusion was unclear on the last job?
services.action: Prepare or review quantities and estimated material costs for trade/GC approval.

services.name: Get supplier quotes
services.when: Time spent comparing suppliers or uncertainty about matching prices.
services.question: How did you compare the last quotes, including matching specifications, delivery and terms?
services.action: Compare like-for-like supplier quotes and negotiate approved material pricing.

services.name: Order through Avantia
services.when: Repeated supplier calls, payments or delivery arrangements.
services.question: Which supplier conversations, payments or arrangements did you personally handle on the last order?
services.action: Arrange approved purchases, supplier payments and delivery coordination.

services.name: Shortages & reorders
services.when: Missing items and repeated calls from subs.
services.question: Tell me about the last missing item: who identified it, approved it and arranged the reorder?
services.action: Receive a confirmed shortage list from the GC/sub and coordinate the approved reorder.
